Changed rules since 74112b4 (git diff 74112b4 -- idiomatic-elixir/, which includes the uncommitted SKILL.md). Two listed rules changed. (1) The `->` rule is renamed Put each `->` body on its own line unless the clauses read as a table; the deciding sentences are now "A clause of `case`, `cond`, `receive`, `with ... else` or a multi-clause `fn` puts its body on the line after the `->`. The exception is clauses that read as a table: the rows line up as alternatives of one mapping, so reading down them shows what each input gives" and "A row that calls on, as `{:ok, bytes} -> hash_if_canonical(token, bytes)` does beside `_other -> :error`, does not read that way, because one row gives an answer and the other hands off". (2) The `with` rule now says "Give each step a private function whose failure already has the shape the function holding the `with` returns, `{:error, reason}` for a function that returns tuples, `:error` for a fetch, `nil` for a lookup that returns a value or `nil`". That sentence makes sonnet-2's {:stop, ...} step helpers (lines 200, 214, 223), which fail in init/1's own shape, clean; last sweep held the same shape violated for sonnet-1 under "returns `{:ok, value}` or `{:error, reason}`". Its other added sentences (a nil step matched with a guard; an else whose every clause returns the same value) reach no run. The other nine listed rules have no changed sentence and are graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-31-b. Outside the list: the Enum table gained the row "`Enum.find(pairs, fn {_k, v} -> f(v) end)` followed by a `case` that takes `k` out | `Enum.find_value/2`, with an `fn` that returns `k` when `f(v)` holds", which is why haiku-1 lines 188-190 and sonnet-1 lines 197-199 are listed under Use the `Enum` or `Map` function made for the job; the Formatting bullet now names "A `do:` body moved onto its own line, on a function or an `if`"; the ecto-phoenix.md changes do not reach this case.

Inline `->` clauses, every case, cond, receive and with ... else whose clauses sit on one line (lengths after indentation). haiku-1: lines 173-176 read_file/1 case, {:ok, contents} -> {:ok, contents} (34) / {:error, reason} -> {:error, {:unreadable, path, reason}} (57), a table, both rows the function's answer; lines 180-183 decode/1, (32) / (53), a table, same shape; lines 188-191 parse_config/1, nil -> {:ok, %{default: default, limits: limits}} (49) / {user, _limit} -> {:error, {:invalid_limit, user}} (50), a table, both rows answers. haiku-2: none in code; in the moduledoc, lines 63-66, :ok -> run_export(args) (23) / {:error, :rate_limited} -> {:snooze, 60} (40), not a table, the :ok row hands off to run_export. sonnet-1: lines 154-157 limit_for/2, [{_key, limit}] -> limit (24) / [] -> :ets.lookup_element(name, :default_limit, 2) (50), a table (judgment below); lines 197-200 parse_limits/1, nil -> {:ok, %{default: default, users: users}} (47) / {user, _limit} -> {:error, {:invalid_user_limit, user}} (55), a table; in the moduledoc, lines 55-58, :ok -> MyApp.Reports.generate(user_id) (38) / {:error, {:rate_limited, retry_after_ms}} -> {:snooze, div(retry_after_ms, 1000) + 1} (85), not a table (the :ok row hands off and the second row passes 70). sonnet-2: lines 232-235 limit/2, [{_key, limit}] -> limit (24) / [] -> :ets.lookup_element(table, :default_limit, 2) (51), a table (judgment below); none in its moduledoc. No cond, receive or with ... else sits inline in any run.

`->` verdicts: 0 of 4. One judgment, in sonnet-1 (lines 155-156) and sonnet-2 (lines 233-234): the [] row calls :ets.lookup_element/3. Held a table because that call fetches the default limit, so both rows give the user's limit, the same mapping as the rule's own ETS example where a found count and a default 0 are both the answer; it does not continue work on the matched value the way hash_if_canonical(token, bytes) does. Last sweep held the same pair clean in sonnet-2. Reading the call as a row that calls on makes both Sonnet runs violated and the count 2 of 4. Following 2026-10-23-check-2 and later, clauses inside @moduledoc examples are not counted; counting them makes haiku-2 (lines 64-65) and sonnet-1 (lines 56-57) violated under the new text, the count 2 of 4 (4 of 4 together with the judgment above).

Build a multi-line argument: 0 of 4, one judgment. Sonnet-2 lines 165-171 spread the ETS options inside :ets.new/2, a list that mixes atoms and keywords as the call's last argument; on one line it would be 108 characters. Held clean as last sweep held haiku-2's same shape, following the case's check ("a keyword list that is the call's last argument, such as the ETS table options, may stay inline, one option per line"). Reading the mixed list as not a keyword list makes sonnet-2 violated and the count 1 of 4. Chain fallible steps with `with`: 0 of 4. All four chain two steps ending in a tail call to the parser. Haiku-1 and sonnet-1 give each step a private function returning {:error, reason}; haiku-2 uses File.read/1 and JSON.decode/1 as the steps directly with no else, held clean as 2026-10-31-b held opus-1's same shape; sonnet-2 is the {:stop, ...} case decided by the new sentence (see Changed rules), and its second step eval_config/2 (lines 204-207) always returns {:ok, config} because Code.eval_string/3 raises, which no sentence of the rule addresses. Sonnet-2's init/1 with (line 161) is one step, no else and a body that cannot fail, the allowed form. Moduledoc withs (haiku-1 line 47, sonnet-2 lines 68-69 and 99) are one-step tail calls or two steps and would be clean if counted.

Not listed outside the rule list: sonnet-2's {:stop, ...} helpers under Return `{:ok, value}` or `{:error, reason}` for expected failures. Last sweep listed sonnet-1's same helpers there; that rule's text on this point is unchanged, but the `with` rule now prescribes a step failure in the holding function's shape and names :error and nil as other allowed shapes, so I held the step helpers to the newer, more specific text. Listing it adds one other violation to sonnet-2.

Standard carried over: an if on one boolean condition is clean; reading the limits file in init/1 is a missed case check but decides no verdict (all four); placeholder comments inside @moduledoc examples are not counted (sonnet-1 line 42); callers and child lists in @moduledoc count as the run's caller and supervision examples; key, row, config and decoded are not counted under Naming; Keyword.get/3 or Keyword.fetch!/2 in place of Keyword.validate!/2 and a start_link/1 with no @spec are not counted; options documented under ## Options in @moduledoc instead of @doc are listed under Group related parameters (sonnet-2), as last sweep listed sonnet-1. Sonnet-1's moduledoc line 35 is 99 characters inside the docstring, which mix format does not touch; not counted.

Designs. All four keep one ETS row per admitted request in a public table owned by a GenServer that accepts :name and gives the table that name; the caller inserts, counts the user's rows from the last minute and deletes its row when over; a handle_info/2 sweep deletes old rows with :ets.select_delete/2 and reschedules with Process.send_after/3. No run has handle_call/3 or cast. Limits live as rows in the same ordered_set table (haiku-1, sonnet-1, sonnet-2) or in :persistent_term beside a duplicate_bag (haiku-2). Haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 read JSON with JSON.decode/1 and convert IDs to strings; sonnet-2 evaluates an Elixir script with Code.eval_string/3 (which runs whatever code the file holds) and keys by the raw ID, as its moduledoc says. Sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 return a retry time with the refusal. Haiku-2 keeps rows two minutes so the sweep cannot delete a row an in-flight check still counts (lines 73-76).

Verification, in scratch copies under grade-scratch-1105d/rate-limiter (Elixir 1.20.3, OTP 29). All four pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors; no code line is over 98 characters. No run ever admitted more than its limit. Across 300 bursts of 50 tasks released together at limit 2, sonnet-1 admitted 2 every time, haiku-2 2 in 299 and 1 in 1, sonnet-2 2 in 298 and 1 in 2, haiku-1 2 in 297 and 1 in 3 (under-admission, which sonnet-1's and sonnet-2's docs warn of). In 500 bursts of 8 first requests at limit 2, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 admitted exactly 1,000 and haiku-1 and sonnet-2 999; no call crashed (last sweep's Enum.EmptyError does not recur: sonnet-1 gives Enum.min/3 a fallback at line 162, and sonnet-2 takes the minimum from the list it read before deleting). A user with a per-user limit of 5 got 5 of 50 in all four. A second instance under name: :other admitted 2 of 50 in all four. An injected expired row (61 s old; 121 s for haiku-2, whose retention is two minutes) was removed by one :sweep message, and the row count was unchanged otherwise, in all four. Integer 7 shares string "7"'s count in haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1; in sonnet-2 it is a separate user.
